name: Ball Corporation
description: Ball makes aluminum beverage cans and ends and sells them under multi-year supply contracts to drink fillers, chiefly beer and soft-drink companies; AB InBev was 15% and Coca-Cola bottlers 14% of 2025 net sales. It is the largest can maker in North and Central America (about 36% of shipments), EMEA (about 39%) and South America (about 46%), per its 10-K. Most contracts pass aluminum price changes through to the customer, so the segments earn comparable operating margins of about 12% to 15% of sales. The remaining 5% or so of sales is aluminum aerosol containers and recloseable bottles (Personal & Home Care), plus can plants in India and Myanmar. It sold its aerospace division in February 2024, which is why 2024 net earnings ($4,008M) dwarfed 2025 ($912M).

gics.note: Conventional filing: sector and sub-industry from Wikipedia's List of S&P 500 companies (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies, read 2026-09-30); industry group and industry not on that page, so null. EDGAR SIC 3411 (Metal Cans). Ball is effectively a pure aluminum beverage can maker since it sold its aerospace business to BAE Systems on 2024-02-16 for $5.6B.

hq.note: FY2025 10-K: 'We are headquartered in Westminster, Colorado'; EDGAR business address is also Westminster, CO; Wikipedia's S&P 500 list says Broomfield, Colorado (see conflicts)

employees.note: About 16,000, including about 5,000 in the US (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Beverage Packaging, North and Central America
businessLines.how: Fillers of carbonated soft drinks, beer and energy drinks buy cans under multi-year supply contracts priced per can; aluminum cost is passed through in most contracts, so profit depends on volume, plant utilisation (plants run more or less continuously) and price.
businessLines.description: Aluminum beverage cans and ends made in 17 US plants, one in Canada and two in Mexico, plus three equity-method investments; Florida Can Manufacturing acquired Q1 2025.

operatingProfit.note: FY2024 $747M on $5,619M; FY2023 $710M. Share is of the three reportable segments' $1,594M. Q2 2026 net sales $2,006M vs $1,613M; H1 2026 $3,782M vs $3,076M.

businessLines.marketShare: Ball shipped about 50 billion cans in the region in 2025, about 36% of about 139 billion units; five companies make substantially all aluminum beverage cans in the US, Canada and Mexico (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Beverage Packaging, EMEA
businessLines.how: Beer and soft-drink fillers buy cans under generally longer-term contracts, with aluminum cost passed through and local-currency contracts hedged; volumes peak from May through August.
businessLines.description: Aluminum beverage cans and ends from 19 facilities in Europe plus one each in Cairo, Egypt and Manisa, Turkey.
businessLines.marketShare: Largest producer with an estimated 39% of shipments in a market of about 97 billion containers in the countries it serves (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Beverage Packaging, South America
businessLines.how: Beer and soft-drink fillers buy cans under supply contracts with aluminum pass-through; volumes peak from September through December.
businessLines.description: Aluminum beverage cans from 12 facilities: 9 in Brazil and one each in Argentina, Chile and Paraguay.

operatingProfit.note: FY2024 $296M on $1,951M; FY2023 $266M. Highest margin of the three.

businessLines.marketShare: Largest producer with an estimated 46% of South American shipments in 2025, in a market of about 43 billion containers; four companies make the cans (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Other (Beverage Packaging Other, Personal & Home Care, corporate)
businessLines.how: Same can-sale model in India and Myanmar; Personal & Home Care sells aluminum aerosol and bottle containers to consumer-goods makers (less than 5% of consolidated net sales in 2025).
businessLines.description: Can plants in India and Myanmar (a Saudi Arabian business was deconsolidated in August 2025, keeping a 10% stake; the aluminum cups business was deconsolidated in March 2025), Personal & Home Care (extruded aluminum aerosol containers, recloseable aluminum bottles and aluminum slugs; nine plants), and undistributed corporate costs.
